newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Yeebo agrees debt restructuring proposal.
newsitem.headline: Yeebo agrees debt restructuring proposal.

text.p: Yeebo (International Holdings) Ltd said on Friday it has conditionally agreed to the implementation of a reactivation and recapitalisation proposal made by its non-executive chairman Kenneth Hung.
The proposal included a 10-to-one share consolidation, a rights issue to raise HK$158 million before expenses and a debt restructuring, the company said in a statement.

Ernst & Young has been appointed as the independent accountants since March 1996 after the company became aware of irregularities within the group believed to have arisen from breaches of fiduciary duty of some of its directors, it said.
In the opinion of Ernst & Young, the proposal was the best available option for the group, its creditors and the shareholders, the liquid crystal displays maker said.
Under the proposal, every ten existing issued or unissued Yeebo shares of HK$0.10 each would be consolidated into one new ordinary share of HK$1.00 each.
It also planned to raise about HK$158 million by offering 157.96 new consolidated shares in the proportion of seven new shares for every two consoldiated shares, the company said.
A restructuring of the outstanding indebtedness for the company and its subsidiaries to a group of nine banks would be made immediately following completion of the share offer, it added.
The group's total indebtedness to the bank group amounted to about HK$257.2 million, Yeebo said.

The company would repay not less than HK$36.6 million immediately following completion of the open offer and the balance of about HK$106 million would be formalised by the loan agreement to be entered into between unit Yeebo Semiconductor Ltd and the bank group, it added.

After the implementation of the proposal, the group would have an adjusted net asset value of about HK$140.28 million, representing about HK$0.69 per consolidated share, before taking into account the financial results of the group for the year ended March 31, 1997.
